q: 101. In which year, UN celebrated international peace on?
explain: The UN observed 1986 as the International Year of Peace, aimed at strengthening peace-related efforts worldwide.

q: 102. The United Nations General Assembly has declared 2023 as the -------
options: International Year of Fruits and Vegetables
explain: The UN General Assembly declared 2023 as the International Year of Millets to raise awareness of the health and nutritional benefits of millets.

q: 103. Which period was declared to mark as "World Decade of Indigenous Language" by United Nations?
explain: The UN declared 2022-2032 as the International Decade of Indigenous Languages to draw attention to the endangerment of many indigenous languages.

q: 104. Nepal was attained membership of UNO in ---------
explain: Nepal became a member of the United Nations on 14 December 1955, after its earlier applications were vetoed.

q: 105. When was Nepal elected to the UN Security Council as a non-permanent membership for the first time?
explain: Nepal first served as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council during 1969-1970.

q: 106. Who is the first permanent representative of Nepal to participate in UN General Assembly?
explain: Rishikesh Shah served as Nepal's first Permanent Representative to the United Nations after Nepal's admission in 1955.

q: 107. Who is the present permanent representative of Nepal in UN General Assembly?
explain: As per this reference material, Lok Bahadur Thapa is listed as Nepal's Permanent Representative to the UN.

q: 108. The first Nepalese prime minister to address UN general Assembly is ----------
explain: B.P. Koirala was the first Nepalese Prime Minister to address the UN General Assembly.

q: 109. When did Nepal participate in United Nations peace-keeping force as an observer for the first time?
explain: Nepal first participated as an observer in a UN peacekeeping mission in 1958.

q: 110. In which country did Nepal work as a peacekeeper for the first time under the United Nations?
explain: Nepal's first deployment as a UN peacekeeping troop contributor was in Lebanon.

q: 111. According to UN Peacekeeping Missions Report -2023, Nepal is the ____ largest troops Contributing Country in UN Peace keeping Operations.
explain: As per the 2023 UN Peacekeeping report referenced here, Nepal ranked as the top (1st) troop-contributing country.

q: 112. Of which organization among the following has Nepal become the member at first?
explain: Nepal's earliest membership among these bodies was with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), joined shortly after independence-era engagement with the UN system.

q: 113. When was Nepal became the member of World Trade Organization (WTO)?
explain: Nepal became a member of the WTO on 23 April 2004, becoming the first Least Developed Country to join through full accession negotiations.

q: 114. Nepal first attained the membership of Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) in --------
explain: Nepal joined the FAO on 21 November 1951, prior to its UN membership in 1955.

q: 115. When and under which treaty was SAARC officially established?
explain: SAARC was formally established on 8 December 1985 through the Dhaka Declaration, signed at the first SAARC Summit.

q: 116. Which of the following given dignitaries is/are not the signatories on the Charter of SAARC?
explain: Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh, who first proposed the idea of regional cooperation, died in 1981, before the SAARC Charter was signed in 1985, so he could not be a signatory.

q: 117. Who was first raised the concept of regional, political and economical cooperation in South Asia?
explain: President Ziaur Rahman of Bangladesh is credited with first proposing the idea of regional cooperation in South Asia in the late 1970s.

q: 118. Which one of the following is not an objective of the SAARC charter?
options: To promote the welfare of the peoples of South Asia
To accelerate economic growth in South Asia
To contribute to mutual trust in South Asia
explain: "Maintaining international peace" is a UN Charter objective, not a stated objective of the SAARC Charter, which focuses on regional welfare, growth, and cooperation.

q: 119. For which of following, the SAARC movement was launched?
explain: SAARC was launched with the core aim of promoting regional cooperation among South Asian nations.

q: 120. Which of the following given is/are the principles of SAARC?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lists sovereign equality, territorial integrity, and non-interference in internal affairs among its guiding principles.

q: 121. How many articles are there in Charter of SAARC?
explain: The SAARC Charter, signed in 1985, contains 10 Articles covering objectives, principles, institutional structure, and administration.

q: 122. How many Apex bodies are there in SAARC?
explain: SAARC has 6 recognized Apex bodies representing professional and civil society groups across the region.

q: 123. Which is the executive body of SAARC?
explain: The Standing Committee, composed of Foreign Secretaries, functions as the executive body overseeing programme implementation.

q: 124. In which Article of the SAARC Charter, the principles of the SAARC is mentioned?
explain: Article II of the SAARC Charter lays down the guiding principles of the organization.

q: 125. Which country is not the founder member of the SAARC?
explain: SAARC was founded in 1985 by seven countries; Afghanistan joined later, in 2007, becoming the eighth member.

q: 126. Who are the members of Council of Ministers of SAARC?
options: Ministers of foreign affairs of the members state
Ministers of prime ministers of the members state
Ministers of defence ministers of the members state
Ministers of home ministers of the members state
explain: The SAARC Council of Ministers comprises the Foreign Ministers of member states and meets to formulate policy.

q: 127. Who is the Nepali artist to design the SAARC emblem?
explain: The SAARC emblem was designed by Nepali artist Shailendra Kumar Mahrajan.

q: 128. When was the 18th Summit of SAARC in Kathmandu held?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit was held in Kathmandu, Nepal from 26-27 November 2014.

q: 129. During the 18th SAARC Summit, which theme has been agreed by all eight member countries by engaging in formal agreement?
explain: At the 18th Summit in Kathmandu, all eight members signed the SAARC Framework Agreement on Energy Cooperation (Electricity).

q: 130. When did SAARC Convention on preventing and combating Trafficking in women and children for prostitution signed in Kathmandu?
explain: The SAARC Convention on Preventing and Combating Trafficking in Women and Children for Prostitution was signed at the 11th SAARC Summit held in Kathmandu in 2002.

q: 131. When was SAFTA (South Asian Free Trade Agreement) signed during 12th Summit in Islamabad on?
explain: SAFTA was signed on 6 January 2004 at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad.

q: 132. When was SAARC framework agreement for energy Co-operation signed on?
explain: The SAARC Framework Agreement on Energy Cooperation was signed on 27 November 2014 during the 18th Summit in Kathmandu.

q: 133. Afghanistan participated as the 8th member of SAARC?
explain: Afghanistan formally joined SAARC as its eighth member during the 14th SAARC Summit held in New Delhi in 2007.

q: 134. Which SAARC summit envisioned the established of South Asian economic Union (SAEU)?
explain: The 18th SAARC Summit's declaration reaffirmed the long-term vision of moving towards a South Asian Economic Union (SAEU).

q: 135. When was South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA) come in force?
explain: Although SAFTA was signed in 2004, the agreement formally came into force on 1 January 2006.

q: 136. Where was the first summit of SAARC held in?
explain: The first SAARC Summit was held in Dhaka, Bangladesh in December 1985, where the SAARC Charter was adopted.

q: 137. Which SAARC Summit decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund (SDF) as a comprehensive funding mechanism with the provision of three windows (Social, Economic & Infrastructure)?
explain: The 13th SAARC Summit (Dhaka, 2005) decided to establish the SAARC Development Fund with Social, Economic, and Infrastructure windows.

q: 138. SAARC is observing a decade (2010-2020) of which of the following?
explain: SAARC declared 2010-2020 as the Decade of Intra-regional Connectivity to strengthen physical, economic, and people-to-people links.

q: 139. What was the theme of the SAARC year 2016-17 A.D.?
explain: SAARC observed 2016-17 as the 'Year of Cultural Heritage' to promote the region's shared cultural legacy.

q: 140. Currently, How many SAARC regional centers are in existence?
explain: SAARC originally had 11 regional centres, later consolidated and reduced to 5 to improve efficiency.

q: 141. Which SAARC Summit decided to reduce regional centre to from 11 to 5?
explain: The decision to consolidate SAARC's 11 regional centres into 5 was taken at the 18th SAARC Summit in Kathmandu (2014).

q: 142. Where is the head quarter of SAARC Chamber of commerce and industry located?
explain: The SAARC Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SCCI) has its headquarters in Islamabad, Pakistan.

q: 143. Where is SAARC cultural centre located?
explain: The SAARC Cultural Centre is located in Colombo, Sri Lanka.

q: 144. Comparing the following Regional Centers established in the SAARC nations; choose the correct answer from the code. a.Nepal b.Bangladesh c.India d.Pakistan / 1.Agricultural Centre(SAC) 2.Environment & Natural Disaster(END) 3.Energy Centre(SEC) 4.Tuberculosis Centre(STC)
explain: Nepal hosts the Tuberculosis Centre (STC), Bangladesh hosts the Agricultural Centre (SAC), India hosts the Environment & Natural Disaster centre (END), and Pakistan hosts the Energy Centre (SEC): a-4, b-1, c-2, d-3.

q: 145. Which of the following is\are not the observer of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC observers include Japan, USA, South Korea, China, EU and others, but the UK is not among SAARC's observer states.

q: 146. How many Country/Organization that granted for the observer status of South Asian Association for Regional Co-operation (SAARC)?
explain: SAARC has granted observer status to 9 countries/organizations, including Australia, China, EU, Iran, Japan, South Korea, Mauritius, Myanmar, and the USA.

q: 147. Who was the first Secretary General of SAARC?
explain: Abul Ahsan of Bangladesh served as the first Secretary-General of SAARC from 1985 to 1989.

q: 148. Who is Current Secretary General of South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC)?
explain: As per this reference material, Golam Sarwar is listed as the current Secretary-General of SAARC.

q: 149. Considering the area of the SAARC nations, which of the following is the right order of those Nations, from the smallest to the largest?
options: Maldives, Bhutan, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, India
Bhutan, Maldives, Nepal, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Pakistan, India
Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India
explain: By land area, the correct ascending order of SAARC nations is Maldives, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, India.

q: 150. Which of the following SAARC country with highest average population growth rate?
explain: Among SAARC countries, Bhutan is cited in this reference as having the highest average population growth rate.
